facts.text: Mickey died three weeks before the new owner, his nephew, came to Quay Street.
Mickey died of his heart, at the office early one morning; Ron found him when he came on at the rank, and the doctor said it was his heart.

Last November, on a Saturday night, the importer's warehouse at the far end of the old warehouse row burned down; the evening paper called it arson, since it started in two places, but nobody was charged, and the street says the owner had it done for the insurance.
Mickey left the office, Mickey's, the cab office on Quay Street, to his nephew, the new owner, by his will; the new owner came with one suitcase and a letter saying so.
Mickey's funeral was at Father Walsh's chapel, before the new owner came; he missed it.
June, Mickey's daughter, came back to the Hook for the funeral and is still in town; she wants nothing from the office.
The new owner is living in Mickey's flat over the office.
The door at the back of Mickey's that Sheila does not open is Mickey's own room; it has been locked since he died, and Sheila keeps the key.
Mickey's has two cab drivers on the rank, one by day and one by night, and a dispatcher on the radio and the phone.
The cab office opens at seven in the morning, nine on Sundays, and runs until the night driver goes home at three.
Mickey's has not made much money since the docks went; trade has been thin.
The cafe is across the street, in the shops opposite the north end of the parade; it opens at half past six and shuts at ten at night, and on Sundays it is open only from eight till twelve.
Mickey's, the minicab office, is on Quay Street in the Hook, with the rank outside.
Sheila Dunn has kept the books at Mickey's for thirty-one years.
Ron Kirby keeps the rank outside Mickey's and watches the yard gate; Mickey kept him on when the docks let him go in 1989.
Darren Milner walks Quay Street at all hours and talks to everyone; if something is being said in the Hook, he has heard it.
Mickey kept his business to himself; you would not hear it from him on the street.
Mickey kept Ron on when the docks let him go in 1989.
